status.label: Reproduce resume-time zone geometry
status.detail: Zero-spacing multi-monitor layouts gain gaps after hibernation; several related reports explicitly duplicate into this issue.

next_action.label: Compare saved spacing and restored window bounds
next_action.reason: Measure zone geometry versus native window borders instead of treating the reporter's hardcoded-margin theory as proven.

judgment.rationale: The multi-monitor, zero-spacing, hibernate/resume sequence is actionable and this issue is the canonical target of several explicit duplicates. The exact layout-selection or window-frame mechanism remains unresolved.
evidence: The report names 0.81.1 and says windows gain margins after hibernation and require resnapping.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/24617 was explicitly closed into #33548 and describes settings still showing no border despite the visible gap.
https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/43923 and https://github.com/microsoft/PowerToys/issues/44321 explicitly close into #33548 for resume-time size/position changes.
Current FancyZones.cpp processes WM_DISPLAYCHANGE through OnDisplayChange and UpdateWorkAreas; this identifies an investigation boundary, not a proven defect.
judgment.recommended_action: Reproduce resume with zero spacing and compare active layout identity, saved spacing, computed zone rectangles and actual window frame bounds.

fix_assessment.rationale: No concrete fix appears in the inspected issue timeline. Closed related reports are duplicate-routing or no-longer-reproducing outcomes, not proof that this canonical issue is fixed.

proposed_fixes.title: Preserve layout geometry through monitor resume
proposed_fixes.root_cause: Hypothesis: transient monitor/work-area reconstruction on resume selects stale layout geometry or applies spacing/frame adjustments inconsistently. Zero spacing must remain distinct from an absent/default value. A hardcoded 15-pixel margin is only the reporter's speculation.
plan: On a two-monitor test system, record active layout IDs, spacing/show-spacing values, DPI/work areas, zone rectangles and window extended-frame bounds before and after hibernate.

Trace src/modules/fancyzones/FancyZonesLib/FancyZones.cpp OnDisplayChange/UpdateWorkAreas and the selected layout/work-area mapping. Determine whether the saved layout changes, zone geometry changes or only the restored outer frame shifts.

If reconstruction loses the selected layout or explicit zero spacing, preserve that mapping/value across transient display states and recompute only against the final valid work area. If zone rectangles remain correct, fix the demonstrated DPI/frame conversion instead of changing spacing defaults.
Add targeted resume/topology and explicit-zero-spacing regressions, including mixed DPI, custom layouts and the option to keep windows in zones when display resolution changes.
verification: Hibernate/resume a zero-spacing multi-monitor layout: saved values and active layout remain unchanged and windows return to the correct bounds.
Resnapping must not be necessary to remove newly introduced gaps.
Nonzero spacing, mixed DPI, KVM/display reconnect and spanning layouts retain intentional spacing; compare zone rectangles with extended-frame bounds.

confidence.rationale: The resume/topology boundary is supported by multiple explicit duplicates, but geometry measurements must distinguish layout reconstruction from native frame/DPI effects.

issue_context.summary: After hibernation in a multi-monitor setup, windows previously snapped with zero margins gain visible gaps until resnapped.
known_information: The report names PowerToys 0.81.1 and multiple monitors.
The hardcoded-margin explanation is a commenter hypothesis, not measured evidence.
Reports #24617, #43923 and #44321 explicitly consolidate into this issue.
The issue remains open, unassigned and Priority-1.
inferences: Monitor topology changes and restoration geometry are plausible common boundaries.
Visible gaps can arise without the saved spacing setting changing, so a settings-only fix may miss the defect.
issue_context.analysis: This is the canonical open report, not a duplicate to close elsewhere. The remaining work is a maintainer-side geometry comparison with sufficient public steps; no generic diagnostic request is necessary for this pass.
initial_investigation: Read the report and both comments.
Read #24617, #23588, #18103 and #17152; distinguish explicit duplicates, KVM symptoms and an old reporter's no-longer-reproducing closure.
Verified current upstream OnDisplayChange/UpdateWorkAreas ownership. Existing drag-lifetime guards are unrelated evidence and do not establish a spacing fix.

reproduce.title: Hibernate/resume changes snapped window bounds
reproduce.version_requirement: Compare reported 0.81.1 with a current supported build.
prerequisites: Two physical monitors; record resolution, scaling and connection types
A custom layout with spacing disabled or explicitly zero
Record the keep-windows-in-zones-on-resolution-change option and preserve original layouts.
steps: 1. Snap test windows into the zero-spacing layout and record active layout ID, saved spacing, zone rectangles and window frame bounds.
2. Hibernate the machine, resume and wait for both monitors to become available.
3. Before resnapping, compare saved settings, active layout and measured window/zone geometry.
4. Resnap once as a control, then repeat with nonzero spacing and mixed DPI to locate the first incorrect conversion or layout choice.
reproduce.expected_result: Resume preserves the chosen spacing and window-to-zone geometry without manual resnapping; measurements distinguish changed zones from shifted window frames.

actions.label: Review resume-time geometry plan
actions.note: Select layout-value preservation or frame conversion only after geometry comparison; no arbitrary margin constant is assumed.
